utterances.text: Captain, with the assistance of the usher, could you take your marker and place on this map where in Knin the photograph depicted in 299 was.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. Somewhere in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you went through that town on the 6th, was the town still burning from the 4th, or was it burning at all?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Individual houses were burning. And down along the main road prior to getting to the parliament, there was six -- approximately six very, very large stores, huge, about two to three storeys. That entire part was burning and then odd houses -- the POL facility was burning throughout -- and odd houses throughout the entire town as we drove around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And was there burning that you observe that came from the 4th and the 5th shelling?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a video, if I may, if I can show you 1D26-0059 from HTV of the 5th of August. Are you familiar with this position up at the fortress?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, there is no audio on this. It is just a video, itself, from HTV on the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the street you were talking about. You were saying you saw there was burning from the 4th and 5th on that street?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. On the right-hand side, which would be the side closest to where the soccer field is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we look at this in concert with your testimony, the shelling took place after this that caused burning in this photograph that is not observable as we speak. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you say that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean, this photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can complete the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The area in the video that you saw was -- there was no evidence of it burning, was there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So by the time this was taken on the 5th, the burning on that street was gone, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, there's an assumption in your question, which I'm afraid the witness cannot testify to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see a date of the 5th of August which could be the day on which it was broadcast. It could be the day on which it was filmed. I just don't know, and I take it that the witness, without further information, might not know as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will tell you from the HTV archives, Your Honour, this is the day it was filmed, 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that is not dispute, then I take it we can accept that. If not, then the only thing the Chamber knows at this moment is that the picture shows a date of the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll offer this video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D276 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the burning, Captain, that you observed down the main street, this was in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the parliament buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did the burning continue from the 6th into the 7th?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that location?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that those buildings burned for several days, smouldering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you 1D12-0016, page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not coming up on my screen, Judge. It is on ours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was a cable, Captain, of the 7th of August, 1995, third paragraph down. From the 7th: "Several houses on the outskirts of the city were still burning, but none were on fire in the city proper?" The houses that you are talking about are in downtown Knin, aren't they, by the parliament building?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D277, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D277 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Changing subjects, Captain, to Ivan Juric. You noted in your 1999 statement, which I'll get the right exhibit number as 293, on page 3, that Mr. Juric reported directly to military headquarters in Zagreb. That's at the bottom of that page, if you want it reference yourself.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which statement is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 1999 statement, sir. It's the November 1st, 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, by the way, did Mr. Juric didn't speak English, did he?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some. We could communicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you communicate through a translator?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In this paragraph, you note that he reported directly to military headquarters in Zagreb, right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Above that, you note that it did not appear to you that he was subordinate to anyone in Knin. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then if you turn to your 1997 statement, it notes that -- It's 577679. Go to 679, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Line, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 22. You note that: "So later it become apparent that Major Juric was running virtually everything in the sector." Is that accurate as well?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mean everything, from a police point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were a police point of view?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You, likewise, say, on line 29 going to line 32: "It was just -- I don't know if he actually was a major, but he certainly was controlling it all in the sense that he had more authority over the army. If he was there and the army was there, it was done his way. I saw him talking down officers that I'd seen before. The bottom line is that, if he's there, it's his way." Is that accurate as well?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the one specific instance where he had -- it seemed like he had an exchange with an HV major who was army, the HV major left not with what he had wanted and was doing whatever Ivan had told him to do. That was the major that did not want to let me through Pakovo Selo with the Kenyans the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you also had the experience at the Akashi meeting where he was telling the colonel what to do?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you note at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, at 683, line 20: "Juric was the guy. He was the guy in Knin and Sector South, period. And I don't believe for a second anything happened without his knowledge or approval." That's accurate as well?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the connotation of police operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in that context, sir, if we turn our attention to some of the latter pages in this document, and if we turn to 7741 and 7742, in line 22, you were asked whether Juric could have stopped looting and burning. Line 22: "So to say he could have stopped it, yes, I guess he could have. But did he know about it? Did he have the resources to stop it? If you tell him that it is his job to control the sector and to go and eliminate the remnants of the Serbs in the hills in Bosnia, and then you say and also to stop looting, well, if you only have so many men, you have to prior advertise your job. "And based on the list I just gave you, I would put looting at the bottom of the list. So when my commander asked me, 'How are things going?' 'There's no more resistance in the hills, sir, and I have completely controlled the sector.' That's how it would work." "Question: Did Juric know about the arson and the looting?" Your answer: "Well, he drove around just like me, so he saw it. He saw it. Well, he had to. He drove to almost every place I drove, as I have related. I met him in places. He saw Kistanje. He saw other places. He was there, so he saw exactly what I saw. He was there, so he saw exactly what I saw." "Did you talking about burning and looting with Juric?" "No, it was obvious. He knew and I knew." So at the time, Captain -- let me slow down a bit. Did you conclude, one, that Major Juric didn't have enough men to stop the looting and the burning?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You did conclude, however, that he must have known about it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the looting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The looting and the burning.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now just going through there quickly, sir, the looting and the burning, I mean, you note an instance in your report at - let me see - 661 at line 23. This is your statement of P292.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Line 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At 23, you say: "Actually, when we got there, there was a guy steel ago car, and a SIS guy told him basically to get out of the area and the guy left right away."

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, I mean, did that indicate to you that this soldier was, in fact, doing something that he wasn't supposed to be doing per military regulations?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the soldier stealing the car?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the SIS officer telling him to stop doing it, and he left.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did it indicate to you that he was doing something that was outside of his military activities?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm. I don't know how to respond. He saw him doing something he told him to stop, get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the SIS guy doing something outside of his military activities. I'm talking about the person stealing the car, the soldier?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge if taking that car was outside of the realm that he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for us, in your proofing statement, that while this looting was going on, that it was not done according to any particular plan. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I saw, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, sir, can I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the spirit of moving through, you don't know what the HV response was to combat this looting, do you? You don't know what steps they took?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will offer, up across the bar, a series of documents on that score. We will just move it. We will discuss it with Counsel for the Prosecution, but in the interest of time, we will just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the advantages from tendering from the bar table is that you can do it at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes, it is more logical than others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I take it that you follow the logic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I bring up D66.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I could just turn your attention, this is a cable from the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go do downtown Knin, the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It talks about the shelling, and it says: "A few downtown buildings and residential areas show shell damage." I'm interested in the, "However." "However, virtually every shop window in downtown Knin had been deployed. There were visible signs of lotting, but a great deal of merchandise remained." "The most obviously looted stores were clothing stores, and it is quite possible that the clothing had been taken by departing residents who had been departed with little opportunity to pack. Police had already been posted downtown to deter looting. And the political officer did not observe any looting activity, although the soldiers did appear to have large quantities of beer at their disposal. A guard was also posted to guard the Serbian Orthodox church." Was it your experience, Captain, that the looting ultimately stopped?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And -- excuse me, in Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And would it have been approximately --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In your recollection, would it have been approximately the 14th/15th of August time-frame, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General Leslie testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is 28 April, 2008, page 2189, lines 15 to 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then he noted: "And the initial troops which showed up at our front gate didn't stay very long, and I can deduce why because they were continuing the advance. Those were front line troops continuing the advance in pursuit of the retreats Serbs." Do you agree with that, Captain, that the soldiers that initially came to the UN camp on the 5th did not say very long but left to pursue the Serbs going north?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I observed, initially it was the Pumas, and they were later replaced by the Tigers in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe, in order to safe others time, in looking at the transcript of the 28th of April, page 2189, it appears on the 24th of April, in my system at least. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I'm going to blame Mr. Misetic for that, because he is responsible for the day. I'm kidding. I apologise, Judge. I do believe the page reference is the same. I took it off the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise on the date, Captain. Just going back to my initial question, though, do you agree that those initial front line troops left Knin very quickly to go after the Serbs after they had taken Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I want to just go through some of these photographs quickly with you that went -- that you had discussed on the -- on the Prosecution case. Let's turn our attention to the 305 series, first. While they are bringing this up, Captain, you noted for us that, as you went up these roads, you saw and followed the path of the Serbs who evacuated. You saw tanks and other types of items, right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you -- and I don't have the transcript, but you mentioned something about fighting and then moving?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you just explain that manoeuvre just a bit.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting at the intersection with Otric, there was a huge ammunition dump, for lack of a better term, in a field; crates and crates, six, seven feet high. And from there, you go north straight up the road, and what we would find is every three, 400 metres, every kilometre, there would be a big pile of ammunition by the side of the road. And as you saw in one picture, actually the rounds are laid out. So it appeared as if the Serbs, as they were going back, they were falling on to the ammunition, using the ammunition to fire, to fight, and continuing back as the Croats were pushing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you, likewise, observe tanks, Serb tanks, that had been abandoned and then were pointed back on the road?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did that indicate to you that they were fighting oncoming troops?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their muzzles were -- sorry. Their muzzles were pointed towards the direction the Serbs were advancing -- correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you complete your answer. If need be, Mr. Kehoe will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think I asked: Did it indicate that they were fighting oncoming Croats, and I think -- you can correct it, Captain.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The muzzles of the Serb tanks were pointing back down in the direction the Croats were advancing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't know the exact series, but I'm looking at 65 ter 4910 which is part of this series.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, it's coming up. I think it is 4910, 65 ter. It's the one with the crushed car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this particular crushed car, sir, you don't know who crushed this car, do you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If tanks were, in fact, retreating quickly, they would go over anything in their way, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't speak to how they retreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the tanks that you found abandoned by the Serbs, you didn't find any T-80s or T-84s, did you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me go to the series of photographs 1D26-0003, 1D26-0016. These are a series of your photographs, Captain. If we can go through these quickly, Captain, with the designation 06148001 on the photograph, that's an ARSK tank that you saw by the side of the road?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photograph --

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, that was not on that evacuation route, that particular tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next one. Tell us about that one, where that one was?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that's, again, an abandoned Serb --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- that you took -- that was on one of these routes that you took?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next one. Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was, I believe, the 95 Brigade, ARSK Brigade in Vrlika. We went back, I can't recall the date, I believe it is the 12th. Although I'm not sure on the date, we went back to check. That's where I said there was no damage, but we found this. There was a wire across one of the boxes that led to us believe that it was booby-trapped, so we left and informed the HV engineers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, we're talking about picture 06148004?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this was ARSK material?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next photograph, 0614800 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, this picture will be the picture on which -- I don't know whether you have any additional questions for this afternoon or how you divided your time. But it is now quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What could the Chamber expect as far as cross-examination this afternoon is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will have one very, very brief area, and then I will turn it over to my colleague, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you together will finish well within, let's say, an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, before we adjourn, Mr. Kehoe, if I read a line to you: "The Croatian public announcement to give security guarantees to the Serbs in the region was intended for Western propaganda purposes. The goal of the Croatians is ethnic cleanse the region, to make room for approximately one million Croatian refugees to set up." Are you aware that this text is introduced into evidence this morning by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was going to come in with another Prosecution witness in, I think, not this week, but the next week after that. It is on their 92 ter list as an exhibit to be used, so the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is good because we get a few lines, and then we get a 35-paged document. Of course, that needs certainly further --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I read the document. I was well aware of the document what it was saying about that. I just present to the Court my knowledge that it was on the 92 ter list coming in another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I hope you don't mind that the Chamber asks these questions, in order not that it later --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... No, no. Judge, please. Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... has to find that, one way or the other, you or anyone was taken by surprise --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... the remainder of the content of that document. Mr. Hill, we would like to finish this afternoon, to have your testimony concluded. The only possibility for us was to resume at a quarter past 4.00 this afternoon. Since we were informed that you'd still be available, I take it that you'll join us again at quarter past 4.00. In the meantime, same instruction as yesterday, not to speak with anyone about your testimony whether already given or still to be given. We adjourn and resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 1.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is not yet in. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I address an issue, before the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the witness comes in. Yes, Madam Usher, you're invited -- but there seems to be a problem with some of our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Our training as technicians benefits members of this Chamber. Yes, Madam Usher, could you already get the witness stand by, then, meanwhile, Mr. Kehoe will address the Chamber. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is an issue of 277, and I do thank Your Honour for bringing it to our attention. It was the series of cables that were part of that 1D12 series. We intended, I intended, to introduce the cable from the 7th and not the whole bundle being uploaded that is a subject of a 92 ter. So clarify Exhibit D277, we were offering specifically 1D12-0025 to 1D2-0027, which were the three pages of that cable and Exhibit 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I take it that, because it was is uploaded, all of it is in the system. So, therefore, you should upload then the relevant portion, so that the registrar can replace the earlier uploaded full version by the three pages you wanted to tender. Mr. Russo, that, I take it, does not meet any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Kehoe, since we have a new registrar at this very moment, and not the same as this morning, if you'd write down exactly, on a piece of paper, what you want to be replaced by what, and then also verify that we will verify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the age of electronics, Your Honour, I'm still in favour of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that will not help you, Mr. Kehoe. Madam Usher, is the witness ready to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hill. I never know whether this is a new hearing or the continuation of the morning. But if it is a new one, you are still bound, as would be the case in the other situation as well, by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your evidence. Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. We can move back to the series of photographs that we were talking about this morning, and that series is the 1D26, starting at 0003. That is the photograph that we ended of on, which is a photograph which the numbers 06148005.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Captain Hill. That's the next one.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this photo, what is this, sir, and can you plays this?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: T-34, on the route to Vrlika south. The reason I took I took the picture is you can see on the back deck, there is actually a round that they loaded, and they left the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this is it an ARSK tank?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next photograph with the designation 06148010.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, ARSK T-34.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you give us a location?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one previous, no; this one is the same T-34 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to be careful now because I think we moved to another one now already, so let's turn back to the previous one. Let the witness -- I saw another one. I think your question was about the previous photograph loaded, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think the photograph that I was dealing with had the designation 06148010, and I think it is one before this, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That appears - at least I'm looking at Madam Usher's screen - to be the one, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that was on the road almost to Otric, on the evacuation route; T-34, again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Abandoned?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next photo, ma'am. Madam Usher, this is 0614183.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is it possible we've missed one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kehoe is asking for this one. We had temporarily another one on the screen, but we'll just forget about that for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This on road north towards Otric, as you go towards Donji Lapac. It's ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we move to the next one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hill you said: "As you can see, it's pointed towards the south." I can't see that on the photograph. So you must have a specific reason why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The four tubes, Your Honour, are pointed directly the way, looking right at you, it would fire right at you, the way that is situating there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were coming from the south when you photographed this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, going north.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This next one, sir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we just did the one we were -- I think if we go back one more, please. Okay. 06148019.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Same ARSK T-34 on the evac route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we go to the next photograph, 06148025.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would that be the same?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photograph, 06148026.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is taking a look from behind the T-34 that you just saw. So we have driven pass it, north. If you look south to the way the Croats would say have been advancing up, you could see the trailer. That was somebody's trailer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you could deduce from this that civilians were moving with military?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next photograph, 06148030.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is it possible to make it bigger?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell if that is it APC or if it's a civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is this a photograph that you took, though, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Along the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll move to the next photograph, 06148031.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ARSK T-34, on the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next photograph, 06148042.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not on the route. We found that at a later date up in Glina, when I was tasked on a security detail for the Vojnic refugee camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So this was not in the Sector South area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually, I believe that was up in Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the next photograph, 06148043.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are Sagger anti-tank missiles. They come in a case. They open the case, put them down. They're Russian. They were in a field beside the road. Again, I believe that was Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the next photograph, 06148033.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Somewhat blurry.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an ARSK ammunition truck on the evacuation route north to Donji Lapac. I believe there were several, but I was taking an example of what an ammunition truck looks like when it's been hit, and it explodes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where was this?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the evacuation route, north from Otric to Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, ultimately, we will offer these in to evidence, pulling the two photographs that the witness just said were in Sector North, which are not in this time-frame -- or not in this geographical area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could you upload the series of photographs, give a list of the ones that are remaining, so that a number can be assigned to those series. Perhaps we could provisionally assign a number. Mr. Russo, I take it there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you already provisionally assign a number until they have been finally uploaded into the system.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit number D278, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it then as that for the time being. Could I ask one clarifying question from the witness. Do you have -- of any of these photographs, do you know when tanks were abandoned, when ammunition lorries would have exploded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it would have to have been prior to the 10th, because that was the first time I went by that area and didn't see it. Then, the next day, we actually went up and saw it, so it would be prior to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that it would have been prior to when you have seen it, but.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the sense that I drove by, Your Honour, on the first day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I'm interested in to know is when, for example, this last picture, whether you have any knowledge on whether this explosion of this ammunition truck took place on the 30th of July or the 8th of August, or dates when equipment was destroyed or abandoned. I see you nodding no. That is not on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact date that this occurred to vehicle or those tanks being abandoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just touching on a couple of issues that you raised this morning, and going to your P292 statement of the 1997, at 7706, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have my book, please? Thank you. Line 21?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, line 22: "On the way back ..." Now this is, and I believe you clarify it on the next page, 7707, on line 18, that of the six people, four were soldiers and two were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this orange truck, this VW flat bed, was picking these bodies up?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't know what they were doing with them?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, turning our attention to my last area that I would like to discuss with you. And in your statement this morning, you noted that there were -- was a 4th Guards Brigade in Donji Lapac. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the gas station south of the town, it was the last check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let me ask if you can turn to -- did you have some confusion between the Pumas and the 4th Guards Brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me help you out here. Let's go to 7685, line 15.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In a discussion, there was a question: "Was he brigade commander for the Pumas or the Tigers?" You note: "He would have been, I believe, a Puma, which would be 4 Brigade. I'm not sure."

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, was there some confusion in your mind on the difference between the 4th Guards Brigade and the Pumas?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me take you to your statement of 7600 -- or 7661. Let me get you a line. It's where you note at the top of the page, on line 1: "With the brigades, one was Puma and one was Tiger." So is it your testimony, sir, that in Knin in the early days, both three brigades were in there: The Pumas, Tigers, and 4th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pumas, my understanding; and then Tigers; I don't know at which point 4 Brigade was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, your testimony is that there were three brigades in there, come the 5th, 6th, 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection is after the Pumas left, then the Tigers were in. And I believe that the only time I had a contact with 4 Brigade, to my knowledge, was when I believed the individual who was going to shoot the Serb interpreter was the CO of the 4 Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, the answer to my question is, yes, you maintain that there are, in fact, three brigade there: The 4, the Pumas, and the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At various times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going to Donji Lapac, where you -- where you stated in your testimony that the 4th Guards Brigade was there. If we can go to your -- by the way, when you were up there in Donji Lapac, and I believe this was on the 11th of August according to your testimony, did these guys that were up there in this check-point outside of Donji Lapac, did they have red berets on?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any head gear at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to D74 -- excuse me, D274. I apologise. Page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just blow up the 11th, not quite that much, so he can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 11th is the date that you maintain that you went to Donji Lapac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think it is a little tough to read, Madam Usher, so if we can reduce that so that Captain Hill can read the edges there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you read that okay, Captain?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in that insert, there is no mention of the 4th Guards Brigade, is there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, two things to tender quickly across the bar table. The first is an order of active defence -- excuse me. An order issued by General Cervenko, dated 6 August 1995. And it is 65 ter 2008, 65 ter 2008. If can you make that English one a little more readable, Madam Usher, or smaller, so we can read it. Can we read that -- sorry. He sees different, okay. The first part of this document, Your Honour, is an order that establishes the operative border areas of responsibility of the Split Military Districts, and they're established as set forth in paragraph A between the Split Military District and the Gospic Military District. They go along, Mala Alan, Gracac, Benje Selo [phoen], to Medjak, to Una railway, all within the Split Military District, setting forth the various areas of responsibility. We have taken the liberty of mapping that item, and that is in 1D26-0047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, maps take a lot of time to be uploaded into the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That, Your Honour, is a mapping pursuant to the HV Main Staff along the plotted lines, consistent with the order that was just read which puts Srb in a Split Military District and Donji Lapac in the Gospic Military District. Your Honour, at this time, across the bar table, we will offer 65 ter 2008, which is the order, and the map 1D26-0047.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 2008 will become Exhibit D279, and the map will become Exhibit D280.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D279 and D280 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next two items, quickly across the bar table, Your Honour, are 65 ter 3216. Your Honour, this is an order for the act of defence issued by General Gotovina on 9 August 1995. If we can turn to page 19 of 18 [sic], paragraph 5.4 -- page 19 of 18 pages, yes. Page 9 of 18. I apologise. Page 9 of 18. If we can go towards the bottom of that page 5.4, where it says "4 Guards Brigade." Without reading the whole matter, it notes, on point 5.4: "HV 4 Guards Brigade shall be withdrawn from the front lines in order to take a break, to be replenished, and to get ready for further combat activities. Split military district commander shall have in reserve one HV 4 Guards Brigade infantry battalion reinforced by artillery-rocket and logistic support. The reserve battalion shall be stationed in the Knin barracks. Basic task of the battalion shall be to intervene along the defence directions at risk in Otric, Operative Group area, OG, area of responsibility." This is signed by General Gotovina. His follow-up order on the last battalion is 65 ter 2311, again, across the bar table quickly. This is a daily operations report, an ops report from the next day, 10 August 1995. If we can go to page 3 of 4, again signed by General Gotovina, which notes at the top of the page, "The 4th Guards Brigade." "One battalion of the 4th Guards Brigade is in Knin as a reserve for possible intervention." Your Honour, at this time, across the bar table, we will offer 65 ter 3216 -- I'm sorry. 65 ter 3216 and 65 ter 2311.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 3216 will become Exhibit D281; and 2311 will become Exhibit D282.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D281 and D282 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Kehoe, you do not introduce these exhibits through the witness. You do not put any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask him a question based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we're waiting for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, based on some of the information that we just tendered across the bar table, that you were in Donji Lapac and in a different Operational Group, and the orders of General Gotovina moving the 4th Guards Brigade out, does that call into question your mind, sir, the fact that the whether, in fact, the 4th Guards Brigade was in and around Donji Lapac on August the 11th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, in your testimony yesterday, at page 3747, lines 6 through 13, you were asked a question by Mr. Russo about the makeup of the group of refugees that came into the camp on the 4th. And I'll read you the question and answer, and then have I some questions for you. The question is at line 6: "Mr. Hill, can you give the Court an idea of what the makeup of what this group of refugees was?" "Answer: Women, children, old men, old ladies. There were some military-aged individuals in it, basically people that have come from town. They had some bags, some personal belongings as they came in. "Question: Did you find weapons on any of them? "Answer: Found one AK, one Russian grenade, and several knives on individuals that we searched."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar [sic], could you please call up 3D00-0798. Madam Registrar, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, in front of you is a letter on UN stationary dated August 12th, 1995, and that's UN stationary from your unit at UN HQ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's your signature at the bottom, "J. Hill, Captain"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The letter says: "Subject: Confiscated Serbian weapons." And the first part of the letter says: "Sir, as per your instructions, on the evening of 4 August 1995, UN MP personnel conducted searched of all refugees, including their personal effects, upon entering the camp. To date, the following weapons have been confiscated and are held in my weapons lockup," and there's a list from A through L of these weapons, which include among other things four AK-47 assault rifles with folding stocks, one RPG-18 rocket launcher, one Mauser rifle, among other things. Now, those weren't being carried in by women, children, old men, and old ladies, were they?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be carried in by anyone who was in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that you saw women, children, old men, an old ladies carrying in weapons such as these into the camp?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't see any weapons brought into the camp. Upon searching the individuals and their personal effects, weapons were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is a considerably more amount than one AK and Russian grenade and several knives. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This memo says "this is has been confiscated to date." That goes to the 12th of August. We were also periodically doing sweeps of the refugee camp and finding weapons, as well as searching on an ongoing basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, the letter is dated 12 August.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The letter says: "On the evening of 4 August, UN MP personnel conducted searches ever all refugees." It doesn't say the search continued from the 4th to the 12th, does it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following sentence says: "To date, the following weapons have been confiscated." That's the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the evening of 4 August 1995, UN MP conducted searches of all refugees. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I have a number for this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. Russo? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this become Exhibit D283.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D283 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please call up 3D00-0799.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between question and answer, and answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. Actually, you don't have to pull that one. I will forgo that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, you had these weapons in lockup. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You, yourself, took one of them, however, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Took one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And used one?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it was an AK 47 with a folding stock?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On August 8th and August 10th, when you were at check-points during your tours -- or August 8th and August 9th, the Croatian military personnel at those check-points recognised that weapon, and you got some significant problems as a result of that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall that at one check-point after Kistanje where I met Ivan Juric, and we went past to go to, I believe, Benkovac or where the Kenyan battalion headquarters was, at that check-point, the Croatian army confiscated the weapon because it was Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, I'd like you to refer to your statement P292, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the upper right-hand corner page number would be the last four digits of 7675, for the registrar as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll submit to you that this is from August 8th, and beginning on line -- start at line 17 with the word "We." It says: "We didn't know what the problem was, but there were shots fired against the UN. By this time, it is getting dark. There is no electricity in the town. So he showed me where the problem was. It was behind a building. There was at least 30 military people, soldiers and MPs, around an UN vehicle. There was a Serb interpreter in the car. This is the first time when I approached. This is where I met the brigade commander of what I believe at the time -- at that time was the 4 Brigade. He is very tall. As I approached, they went crazy about our weapons. They've never done that before. I was carrying my AK, a pistol." Mr. Hill, they weren't going crazy about "our weapons." They were going crazy about your weapon, were they not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not the case. As a clarification, when I say "my AK," up until the morning of the 5th, I believe, when the artillery round killed those ARSK soldiers, I had been authorised to carry a Czech Republic AK. Our weapons, the Canadian version of an M-16 called a C-7 is inadequate, and Colonel Leslie at the time authorised us to use the AKs that the Czech were carrying within my unit. I had lost that because my Czechs were caught in Zagreb, so the only solution for me was using the Serb one. So it could be, depending on date, Czech or Serb. At this point, the reason they went crazy, in my view, is they didn't want anyone near their commander with any type of weapon at all, even my pistol which was unusual. I never had turn over a pistol. It's always on my thigh. Both weapons had to be given to my second in command before I could approach the commander. It was irrelevant what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go do 1D17-0213.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the cover sheet, Mr. Hill, for the witness statement of Phillip Roy Berikoff. You know who that is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Berikoff?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, he was an intelligence officer in the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: He was a Canadian military man, was he not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And August 9, you and he were together going towards Benkovac, were you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: What line is that in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to page -- by the way, the statement was dated May 26/27th of 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let go to page 0234 of that same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And we'll start on line 18: "On the 9th of August, Captain Hill and Captain Dangerfield, Sergeant Green, Corporal Tremblay, and I once against pushed the restriction of movement envelope, and this time we were stopped at a Croat check-point at Bribirske Mostine. We were forced out of our vehicle at gunpoint by a number of intoxicated Croat soldiers. I could not identify their unit because they were not wearing any soldier badges. They were more of a paramilitary organisation at this time. "As I said, we were forced at gunpoint, and the reason for that was actually quite stupid on the part of Captain Geoff Hill. When we backed the soldiers, ARSK soldiers, on the first day of the offensive, a number of weapons were collected and turned into the military police at the UN compound. Captain Hill and Corporal Tremblay decided to each carry an AK because of the folding rifle stock, and use it instead of our regular C-7 rifle. "When we got to the check-point, this intoxicated Croat soldier recognised the rifle that Captain Hill was carrying, and he went ballistic and started yelling and screaming and pointing his gun at us. And the rest of the soldiers surrounded the vehicle and forced us out of the vehicle. We were fortunate enough that there was a Croatian English-speaking officer that had been at the Kenyan headquarters in Bribirske Mostine. He came down and defused the situation. "We were finally allowed to go; however, Captain Hill's weapon was confiscated by the Croat soldier, and finally -- and we finally were told to go back to our headquarters in Knin." Now, Mr. Hill, it's true, is it not, with respect to the AK that the reason the soldiers went nuts was because it was a Serb weapon that you had taken from the confiscated weapons early in the 4th or 5th of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the reason they went crazy the way they did was because the weapon I had was of Serbian origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's the second day in a row that that happened. It happened on the 8th and it happened again on the 9th, because had you an AK that was a Serb weapon, right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second day it happened because it was a Serb weapon. The first day it occurred because ita was a weapon, period; and we were in the presence of a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have that portion of the statement, the title page, and that page marked as a MFI. Mr. Berikoff is testifying, so I guess we can do what we did with Mr. Tchernetsky, if that is agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will follow the same procedure. I don't know whether he is on the witness list, but we will follow the same procedure for this portion of the document, because you do not want to tender the whole of it, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It doesn't make sense at this point, Your Honour, because I didn't put any questions to him about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour, and Mr. Berikoff is on the witness list and will be coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, have you uploaded this portion or is it still to be uploaded just those pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the portion of the document will become Exhibit number D248, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hill, I'd like to ask you some questions now about D267. It was a document that Mr. Kay had asked you some questions about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we go to page 4 of the English version of that document, please, to the lower part after: "I appoint Major Ivan Juric," and a little higher. That's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kay had asked you about Mr. Juric, and you had testified and made -- had several comments in your statements about Mr. Juric and his area of responsibility. Do you know -- strike that? The next gentleman, whose named Colonel Damir Kozic, have you ever met him before?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So if I told you that Colonel Damir Kozic was similarly situated to Major Ivan Juric, but for the areas of Gracac and north, you would not know anything about that, would you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So when you went into Gracac and further north to Korenica on your tour on August 10th, you had no contact with anyone related to Mr. Kozic's staff or group. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you went to the north, you said you ran into some check-points on August 10th. Who were or what personnel were manning those check-points?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which check-points?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The check-points Gracac and north.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you show me where that is in my statement, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you the question: What check-points did you run in, if you ran into any check-points at all, from Gracac and north, up to Korenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you run into any check-points at all on August 10th on your way up from Gracac to Korenica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We can take that document down now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was some testimony about the anti-terrorist unit of the military police that you had. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I this seen when the HV came to the gate for the first time at noon, I believe it was the 5th, and it was the one time I saw what I believed to a counter-terrorist unit member of the HV. That was later confirmed when I had talked to Ivan Juric, that, in fact, that was part of the HV police. It's the only time I saw one of those members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What did they look like?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grey uniform, black belt. The uniform is like one piece, like a tank suit, black boots. This individual had an MP-35 with a suppressor and a laser sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that individual at any other place other than in Knin?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were at various check-points throughout the, let's say, 10th, 11th when you were in Donji Lapac area, what were the people at those check-points wearing.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Donji Lapac was standard HV combat camouflage. I never saw anyone at that check-point dressed like the counter-terrorism unit member.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you questions about Gracac specifically, Mr. Hill, and if we could take a look at the map that you drew your various routes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is P307, if we could pull that up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, unfortunately, my copy is not in colour, so I'm going to have to squint down and take a look at the screen of P307. But on the 10th of August, noted in blue is your trip up to -- toward Pecane and Korenica. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And on that trip, you would have gone through the city of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you need it enlarged, feel free to ask?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you would go north from Knin, get to where the red circled Otric is, and then go left toward Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Or that would be roughly east, north-east?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then from Gracac, you would go and head north, and it is off the map, but Pecane is north of Gracac, correct, at least in this enlargement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could zoom out one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to know from your -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, east, north-east, where exactly is that? I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. My directions, Your Honour, were not very good, and I apologise foot Court and to the witness for that. It is north-west, actually.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's west and then west, north-west from Otric to Gracac. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are invited to be more precise, and you, Mr. Hill, if something is put to you which is not exactly correct, even visible on the screen, then please be very alert on possible mistakes by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My fault, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On P292, I'd like to ask you some questions about your trip through Gracac, Mr. Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 7698 is the page -- actually, 7699. Are we there, Madam Registrar? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Line 17, you were asked a question: "Please correct me if I'm wrong, you said that Gracac was targeted by shelling." And you answer: "Oh, yeah, it was obvious." Then you were asked: "Was there any buildings in particular that you can remember? Were they civilian houses or were they ..." -- And you answered: "To my knowledge, there was nothing in Gracac of military value. It's just a town, another town with the same houses with red roofs. They got basically destroyed." I would like to ask you: Who told you or how did you come to your knowledge that there was nothing in Gracac of military value?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall ever seeing anything prior to the offensive on the 4th that was there with the ARSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So that's not to say that there was, perhaps, nothing of military value. You just didn't know whether there was something of military value. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, that's what the statement says, "to my knowledge." So, therefore. That is already part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back to 7698, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At this point in your statement on August 10th, which is the time-frame you were talking about the debris trail, and on line 10, you said: "At the intersection of Gracac, the debris seemed to stop. We lost the trail. There was a massive ammo dump there to the side of the road where the horse was." Now, the massive ammo dump would seem to be a military target. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say "massive ammo dump," that was crates and crates of ammunition that had been put there in the middle of a field. It was not a building. It was not a structure. It appeared as if ten-tonne trucks would back up, the ammunition was offloaded, and it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is not contained in the next two lines, however, is it? "Artillery rounds were laying everywhere. It was destroyed." I read that right, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I remember seeing artillery rounds with the fuses, laid out there rows and rows and rows. Artillery rounds were laying everywhere. It was destroyed. The ammunition dump was not. I don't know what this is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "Ammo dump" has a common connotation as a depot for ammunition, does it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it not a depot. This was one that was put by the side of the that was fast and temporary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That is not said anywhere in these three sentences. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It is it not said in those three sentences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that Gracac was a fairly significant junction going north, east, and west on the highway between north and south for Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of a Territorial Defence building in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the police station that was in Gracac that was involved in Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of any other military targets in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to pull up 3D00-0387, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: While that is coming up -- actually, I'll wait for it come up and ask the questions relating to that, because it dovetails into this map. Mr. Hill, can you tell me -- I'll represent to you that this is a map of Gracac and its greater locality. The intersection which is toward the right third of the document, of the map, is the intersection that would lead one north towards Korenica, west towards Gospic through Gracac, and east towards Otric. Is this the road that you took when you went through Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you would have -- if you could use the cursor please -- actually, why don't you use the blue marker, and that way we will have a permanent record of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, will you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us the route that you took as you were coming from Otric west towards Gracac on August 10th, and then going north toward Korenica. And if you could mark that in blue with the pen there that the usher provided.

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would only know that I would following this route, unless I can see the map higher, to see if that is a direct shot up north. I can't tell if that was, in fact, the road I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's assume for a moment, and for purposes of this question, that the intersection that you went just beyond is the road that goes directly north to Korenica. Would that have been the road you took?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most direct route, directly north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you would not have gone -- let's assume for a moment that the direct route goes straight north from the intersection that you just passed with your blue marker, that would be the most direct route to Korenica and that is the route you would have taken?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the map I gave of all of the routes, you will see that we always took primary routes, with the exception of when the HV would not let me move, and then we would go secondary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you some a few more questions about this, and then we will try to find another map, Mr. Hill. If you took the most direct route, would you agree with me that you would not have gone through the city of Gracac, itself; you would have gone around it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if you could, please, on your way through Gracac, if you can designate for me, in your statement, you said: "It was destroyed." Tell me, in this map, what was destroyed, if you can, in terms of the area? What buildings, what anything?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destruction in general, some buildings burning, some destroyed by artillery. As you come into the town on the main route, the south side, there was a big field where there was an HV check-point. That's where we saw the artillery impacts in the ground as they were walking into the town of Gracac from east to west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No people present in the village, and an extremely strong smell of dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Circle for me the area that you said was totally destroyed on this -- on this map?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't circle it exactly. The town in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So, for you, the whole town would be from one end of the map to the other?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on where the northern route would be. It would be up to that route a little past and around perhaps south, and then moving up northwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, why don't you just draw a circle around what you say was totally destroyed?

utterances.speaker: JOHN GEOFFREY WILLIAM HILL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I see what the route is I take, then I can do that more accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's assume for a moment you took the route along the road that you said was the most direct route, which was right before you ended your blue mark, for purposes of this question. What was destroyed, if that's the route that you took?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
